name: One-way conduction
description: Heat flow in one direction only: the target's temperature changes at Conductance × (source temperature − target temperature) / Thermal capacitance, and the source is not touched. Connect it from a Temperature boundary (it reads the boundary's Temperature) to a Thermal mass or a Battery (it changes their Temperature). Because nothing flows back, the boundary stays exactly at its starting temperature, which is what makes it a fixed ambient. Conductance (W/K, default 50) is how readily heat moves for each kelvin of difference. Thermal capacitance (J/K, default 1000) is how much heat the target needs to warm by one kelvin; use the target's own value. For two bodies that both change, use Thermal link instead.
